findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached Hungarian endpoint mean-squared-distance and FLOWR endpoint VJP, so no affinity-head derivative or extra model forward is available as evidence.

The observed window is the score-time grid 0.0-0.49 with learning window [0.0,0.5]; recorded affinities were removed and replaced by an equal score prior, so no observed affinity label exists inside the window and last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Terminal metadata place the terminal score time at 0.99 and terminal state time at 1.0, outside the observed window, with one future-resampling node per batch; decoded terminal labels are therefore unavailable to this analysis and the selection-versus-descendant comparison cannot be completed.

The information audit reports 14 independent batches and a compressed-choice excess fixed-frame RMS of about 0.081 A (CI95 ~0.070-0.092) over a fixed RMS of about 0.564 A, but explicitly states this is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian and that nonnegative excess distance is by construction rather than a causal affinity effect.

Teacher-score correlations with the chosen compressed candidate are weak (whole-window mean ~0.10, CI95 ~0.065-0.140) and the audit states these correlations are observational and not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor, so they cannot be used as an absolute reward target.

The curve-support selection rule retained 24 features requiring absolute integrated z >= 0.1, batch direction fraction >= 0.857, q < 0.05 and exclusion of the scale floor, with a fidelity rule of relative RMSE <= 0.35, strong sign-conflict nodes = 0 and quiet-node large-fit fraction <= 0.1; this is a filtered subset, not the full feature population.

Continuous-trend rows for landmark_00 local features show large first-to-last rate reversals (e.g. local_dy first_rate_z ~ -72.4 to last_rate_z ~ +5.5; local_cxy first_rate_z ~ +64.8 to last_rate_z ~ -19.7) with 4-10 sign changes, 1-14 strong sign conflicts and relative node RMSE 0.29-0.87, and no polynomial was accepted and extrapolation is disallowed; these are unstable observed-node linear fits, not validated time-conditioned rules.

Lineage support shows 349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 with fewer than 6 ancestors out of 700 total batch nodes, with at most 2 teachers per batch, so ancestral coverage is sparse and survivor/ancestor-weighted credit is biased toward the minority of well-covered nodes.

The information audit lists explicit limitations: node summaries describe correlated within-batch candidates with uncertainty taken from independent batches, and proper rigid alignment retains fixed Hungarian correspondence rather than a globally solved rotation/permutation distance, so regional or joint claims cannot be upgraded to global pose or shape conclusions.

hypotheses.direction: Prefer signed contrast direction at observed selection nodes for the retained curve-support features; treat the contrast as a coordinate reward, not an absolute geometric descriptor or affinity target.
hypotheses.falsifier: A retained feature whose batch direction fraction falls below the selection threshold or whose sign reverses across independent batches would weaken the proposed direction.
hypotheses.observable: Signed integrated contrast z and batch direction fraction for retained curve-support features at observed score nodes.
hypotheses.scope: Observed window [0.0,0.5], 14 independent batches, retained features only.
hypotheses.statement: Signed favorable-versus-comparison coordinate contrasts at observed selection nodes may carry reproducible directional information over the complete observed window, but only for the 24 features passing the curve-support selection rule and only as observed-node interpolation without extrapolation.

hypotheses.direction: Retain a constant or static contrast rule rather than a time-conditioned rule until a validated fit exists.
hypotheses.falsifier: A feature with an accepted polynomial fit, zero strong sign conflicts and low relative node RMSE would support a time-conditioned rule.
hypotheses.observable: Sign changes, strong sign conflicts, relative node RMSE and polynomial acceptance per continuous-trend feature.
hypotheses.scope: landmark_00 local features, observed window only.
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast rule is not supported over a constant rule by the supplied continuous trends, because the observed-node linear fits show multiple sign changes, strong sign conflicts and no accepted polynomial.

hypotheses.direction: Treat turnover and survival credit as accounting diagnostics only; do not express them as a causal selection effect or atom velocity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Decoded terminal labels with adequate ancestral coverage would allow the within-path versus cohort-composition comparison.
hypotheses.observable: Parent-child increment contrasts, turnover residual and ancestor counts per node.
hypotheses.statement: Within-path coordinate change cannot be separated from changing cohort composition with the supplied evidence, because terminal labels are outside the observed window and ancestral coverage is sparse.

limitations: No observed affinity labels exist in the window (recorded affinities removed, equal score prior), so final predicted target affinity cannot be evaluated from the supplied observations.
Decoded terminal labels are unavailable; terminal score/state times (0.99/1.0) lie outside the observed window, so last-record credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.
The information audit states its metrics are not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian, and that teacher-score correlations are observational, not a validated affinity predictor.
Continuous-trend fits are observed-node linear with no accepted polynomial and extrapolation disallowed; they are unstable and cannot support arbitrary time bins or extrapolation.
Ancestral coverage is sparse (349 nodes with <3 ancestors, 531 with <6 of 700), so survivor/ancestor-weighted credit is biased.

No joint-diagnostics, regional-effects, survival-effects, increment-effects, endpoint-effects, branch-adjusted or turnover-accounting rows were read in this analysis, so coupling, redundancy and multiplicity-adjusted ranking claims remain unsupported here.
No temperature edit is proposed or permitted; temperatures are immutable task parameters.

task.formula: R=tau*logsumexp(log_pi-rho_delta(q)/tau), q=detached-Hungarian endpoint mean squared distance; rho_delta=delta^2*(sqrt(1+q/delta^2)-1). Actual pointcloud_delta_A defaults to 1 A. Native endpoint VJP, no affinity-head derivative, no extra model forward. teacher_neighbors is a count; temporal_recipe changes only a registered scalar/attention, not velocity. No temperature edits. Inert legacy metadata is not a reward term.

formula_registry.diagnostic_limit: Moment effects, pair kernels and turnover are diagnostic evidence. Executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term; legacy robust_delta is inert.
formula_registry.dose: Endpoint-VJP force normalized and RMS-scaled against native predictive update; eta/ramp only in U lane.
formula_registry.prior: Detached nearest-k teachers; log_pi=-q_anchor/prior_temperature; scores beta=0; k is a count.
formula_registry.regional: Detached background plus Gaussian landmark attention; positive surrounding weight.
formula_registry.temporal_region: Same static teachers; validated absolute contrast changes regional attention at observed score nodes.
formula_registry.temporal_teacher: (1-blend)*R_static + blend*R_observed_teacher(time); same shared FLOWR endpoint, no velocity target.

incumbent.topology_policy: Free native graph transitions; no pair-distance acceptance or graph equality veto

task.objective: Final predicted target affinity primary; validity and strain secondary; coordinate control only
task.task_wording: Use these observations to provide your response to the supplied molecular coordinate task.
